THE ARENE IS THE BINDING SPECIES, not a conservative stand-in: the phosphite is the electroactive partner -- the paper forms the C-P bond 'through the reaction of arenes with anodically generated P-radical cations' -- but it is consumed into the product rather than regenerated, so this is not a mediated cycle, and the ceiling is the smaller of the two co-reactant fluxes. Each product takes two electrons whichever partner limits (the phosphite is oxidized first and the adduct radical second), so the phosphite side carries 2 x 0.25 = 0.5 D_P and the arene side 2 x 0.05 = 0.10 D_Ar; with comparable diffusivities the arene binds, so the arene is what this row transports. Its identity in Table 1 is 'benzoate 1', drawn in a scheme and not named in the text; mesitylene, the arene of the paper's own 231-h continuous production run (55.0 g product), is adopted as the named representative at the Table 1 concentration
